column3: “These were the father of Etam” is rendered “these were the sons of Etam”; the Hebrew is difficult.
“Descendants of Hur” is rendered “sons of Hur.”
NASB reads “Izhar” (written text); the reading tradition has “Zohar.”
“The Zobebah clans” is rendered “Zobebah,” and “clans” as “families.”
“If you will bless me” is rendered as a wish (“Oh that You wouldst bless me indeed”), and “brought what he asked” as “granted him what he requested.”
NASB does not have “and Meonothai,” which comes from the Septuagint; “the sons of Othniel” is rendered “the son of Othniel.”
“Ge-harashim” is kept as a name; it means “valley of craftsmen.”
The Hebrew “and the sons of Elah and Kenaz” is rendered “and the son of Elah was Kenaz.”
NASB moves the clause about Bithia from verse 18 into verse 17 (in parentheses) and supplies “and bore.” “The son of Ezrah” is rendered “the sons.”
“Judahitess” is rendered “Jewish”; NASB moves the last clause (about Bithia) to verse 17.
“The father of Keilah” is rendered “the fathers of Keilah.”
“The house of the work of fine linen of the house of Ashbea” is rendered “the house of the linen workers at Beth-ashbea.”
“Ruled to Moab” is rendered “ruled in Moab,” and “the words” as “the records.” The Hebrew is difficult.
“In his service” is rendered “for his work.”
